title: Tenor trombone
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS tenor trombone (model and player are stated as NA on the page)
summary: Limits first: the lip is an artificial latex pair (Cullen 2000), not a player's; each note's pre-stress and slide are set for equal temperament, not for the recordings; and every note is still too dark against the recordings. A tenor trombone on Braden's (2006) 14-element Conn 88H template (a population stand-in, no F attachment), whose pitch is never an input: the note is the lock between lip and bore. The pages carry per-note slide settings, a flow-noise row (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, an extrapolation) and, on most notes, a row that widens the lip opening as the lips part (q = 1.4, one number solved on Bb3 from Copley and Strong's printed areas; it partly stands in for lip swing the model lacks). The graded sound is the radiated pressure of the flanged bell, 1.524 m on axis, rendered at 19.2 kHz.
physics_present: fs-couple brass_loop: a one-degree-of-freedom outward-striking lip island advanced by exact held-force propagation, a Bernoulli aperture solved implicitly with the mouthpiece cup junction, closing on the bore's reflectance
fs-duct multimodal transfer-matrix bore with exact Bessel viscothermal loss, realized as a passive causal line; the bell as Bessel horns expanded into cones lying exactly on their curves

full flanged modal radiation load at the bell, with the listener a finite-distance Rayleigh integral over every mouth mode, 1.524 m on axis, so the graded sound is radiated pressure and not mouthpiece pressure

the lip as printed by Cullen (2000, Table A.2): embouchure 7 on most pages, embouchure 19 on B3 and Ab4 (response measured, rest gap and width estimated by the thesis); pre-stress is a gesture, set per note (the Eb3 page calls its 0.58 a player's setting)
slide settings per note, stated on each page: the printed 4th position (G2), third position with the tuning slide pulled 84 mm (Eb3), and tuning-slide or tube-length changes on the others

flow noise at the mouthpiece from the printed constriction law (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, as reprinted by Guedel 2005): a pressure source in each third octave, sized by the pressure across the lips at that instant and the card's own cup radius; no level was set against a recording

an area-height row: opening = width x height x (height / rest height)^(q - 1), q = 1.4 on the pages that carry it; the form and its normalisation at each lip's own rest height are ours, and q was solved on Bb3 from Copley and Strong's (1996) printed areas, with Bromage, Campbell and Gilbert (2010) printing 1.49 and 1.55 at E3 for an artificial mouth
a blowing-pressure gesture of a 12 kPa attack and a hold on the shared canonical schedule format (Ab4 is held at 12 kPa)
physics_missing: a player's lips: the lip is Cullen's artificial latex pair, outward-striking mode only on every page; human outward resonances are far lower and more heavily damped, and no human lip mass, width or rest gap is published

the lip's swing: against Copley and Strong's printed heights our lip swings too far at the bottom of the range and too little in the middle, so q = 1.4 on Bb3 is partly standing in for swing and should not be read as the lips' area law; fitting the print's own table gives about 1.1 to 1.2, and the lips stay closed a larger share of the cycle than the print's 10 to 15 %
a second, inward-striking lip mode on the pages: the row is landed (lip_response_mode2, ae66a7c66) but no page uses it

the recorded trombone: the Iowa page gives no model, so the Conn 88H template is a population stand-in and the F attachment is absent; its mouthpiece and leadpipe (element 1) are digitized from Braden's Figure 5.3, not a measured table

a printed playing pressure: Copley and Strong print none and Boutin et al. 2015 print 1.4 kPa for notes played mp, so each hold is chosen so the lip speaks (6 kPa after the 12 kPa attack on most pages, 12 kPa on Ab4), and the 12 kPa attack is the card's and not a measurement

a player's slide: C3 and B3 are set with a tube shorter than the template, which a real player does not do (the hand slide goes out), and the template's own slide setting is not known, so read them as notes brought to pitch and not as slide positions

dark sound: every page reads too dark against its recording (centroid well under the recording's), and the flow noise is close to flat with frequency, which is not the recordings' shape; the row is an extrapolation from dampers and plates in a large duct at 10 to 25 m/s
a clock that reaches the bell's radiation ceiling: the render runs at 19.2 kHz and everything above the receiver's resolved band is unmodelled
the microphone: an on-axis listener only; the player's bell orientation, any microphone directivity and any room are not modelled
breath-warmed and humidified bore gas, wall vibration, nonlinear propagation and shock formation at forte (the source of brassiness), mutes, and the slide's own acoustic leakage
a same-specimen impedance pair, so the passive chain is checked only against published population data
blocked: The C3 page cannot take the lip row yet: with the slide out 114 mm it reaches pitch in its last second but speaks near 353 Hz for its first 0.8 s, which is not that note, and the grader refuses it; a softer attack is being tried.
